title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: insights and retention policy recommendations for sensitive SharePoint and OneDrive data
summary: The briefing passes: the planned capability and target dates match the roadmap, and the existing retention-policy path, command and role qualifications match Microsoft Learn. It appropriately leaves the new insights' default, access controls and feature-specific licensing unresolved rather than borrowing requirements from neighbouring features.

claims.claim: Learn describes retention policies as the cornerstone of Data Lifecycle Management.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Existing retention policies cover Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Use these policies for Microsoft 365 workloads that include Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Viva Engage.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Retention policies can retain content.
claims.quote: Configure whether content for these services needs to be retained indefinitely, or for a specific period if users edit or delete it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An administrator can configure an existing retention policy to permanently delete content after a specified period.
claims.quote: Or you can configure the policy to automatically permanently delete the content after a specified period if it's not already deleted.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: A retention policy can combine retaining content and then deleting it.
claims.quote: You can also combine these two actions for retain and then delete, which is a very typical configuration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Existing retention policies are reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies, with New retention policy starting creation.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. ... Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration, and name your new retention policy.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -SharePointLocation "<site URL>" creates a retention policy targeting the specified SharePoint site.
claims.quote: The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy. ... The SharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to include. You identify the site by its URL value, or you can use the value All to include all sites.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: A new retention policy is not valid until a rule is added, so scripting also requires New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). For more information, see New-RetentionComplianceRule.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is a separate role required for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: admins must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. This role isn't included by default in the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[1].scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls

claims.quote: Use a retention policy to manage the data for your organization by deciding proactively whether to retain content, delete content, or retain and then delete the content.
